question_en: Trina Romel, mutual fund manager, is taking over a poor-performing fund from a colleague. Romel wants to calculate the return on the portfolio. Over the last five years, the fund's annual percentage returns were: 25, 15, 12, -8, and –14. Determine if the geometric return of the fund will be less than or greater than the arithmetic return and calculate the fund's geometric return: Geometric compared to Geometric Return Arithmetic
explanation_en: The geometric return is calculated as follows: [(1 + 0.25)(1 + 0.15)(1 + 0.12)(1 - 0.08)(1 – 0.14)]1/5 – 1, or [1.25 × 1.15 × 1.12 × 0.92 × 0.86]0.2 – 1 = 0.4960, or 4.96%. The geometric return will always be less than or equal to the arithmetic return. In this case the arithmetic return was 6%.

question_en: A portfolio's monthly returns follow a distribution with a kurtosis measure of 4.2. Relative to a portfolio with normally distributed returns, this portfolio has a:
option_a: higher probability of extreme upside returns and higher chance of extreme downside returns.
option_b: lower probability of extreme upside returns and higher chance of extreme downside returns.
option_c: higher probability of extreme upside returns and lower chance of extreme downside returns.
explanation_en: A leptokurtic distribution (a distribution with kurtosis measure greater than 3) is more peaked in the middle (data more clustered around the mean) and has fatter tails at the extremes (greater probability of outliers).

question_en: Find the respective mean and the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of a series of stock market returns. Year 1 14% Year 2 20% Year 3 24% Year 4 22%
explanation_en: (14 + 20 + 24 + 22) / 4 = 20 (mean) Take the absolute value of the differences and divide by n: MAD = [|14 – 20| + |20 – 20| + |24 – 20| + |22 – 20|] / 4 = 3%.

question_en: A distribution of returns that has a greater percentage of small deviations from the mean and a greater percentage of large deviations from the mean compared to a normal distribution:
explanation_en: A distribution that has a greater percentage of small deviations from the mean and a greater percentage of large deviations from the mean will be leptokurtic and will exhibit positive excess kurtosis. The distribution will be taller (more peaked) with fatter tails than a normal distribution.

question_en: If a distribution is positively skewed, then generally:
explanation_en: When a distribution is positively skewed the right side tail is longer than normal due to outliers. The mean will exceed the median, and the median will generally exceed the mode because large outliers falling to the far right side of the distribution can dramatically influence the mean.

question_en: Which of the following statements about kurtosis is least accurate? Kurtosis:
option_a: describes the degree to which a distribution is not symmetric about its mean.
option_b: is used to reflect the probability of extreme outcomes for a return distribution.
option_c: measures the peakedness of a distribution reflecting a greater or lesser concentration of returns around the mean.
explanation_en: The degree to which a distribution is not symmetric about its mean is measured by skewness. Excess kurtosis which is measured relative to a normal distribution, indicates the peakedness of a distribution, and also reflects the probability of extreme outcomes.
